headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: HB 1393 directs Virginia's primary electric provider to establish rates requiring data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg.
news_headline: SCC Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) ordered data centers and other large energy users to cover the full cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities, a decision urged by Governor Spanberger's administration. This move is projected to save Virginia families and small businesses hundreds of millions of dollars by preventing these costs from being passed on to them.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: SB 553 requires water users supplying water to data centers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided monthly, enabling better data collection for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, policymakers, water resource planners, environmental groups.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553 and HB 496 to strengthen water-use reporting requirements for data centers, providing better data for state and local planners to understand the industry's impact on water resources. Senator Kannan Srinivasan, a sponsor, highlighted the need for transparency as data centers expand.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: HB 153 establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) requiring site assessments for sound profiles on nearby homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community advocates, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local residents, Governor Spanberger's administration.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law Forces Developers to Study Noise
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining the sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to localities.
